en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Mañjiṭṭhaka Mansion in the Itthivimāna Section.
2. The Mansion of Radiant Splendor “O you who resemble the color of excellent radiance,
clothed in garments of deep red;”
"O goddess of great psychic power, with a body radiant as sandalwood,
who are you, O beautiful one, that pays homage to me?
And this couch of yours is of great value."
Adorned with various jewels and beautiful,
where you sit resplendent like the king of the gods in the Nandana grove.
What good conduct did you practice in the past, O Bhaddā?
Of what karma is this the result that you now experience in the world of the gods?
“O deity, being questioned, tell me:
what is the fruit of this deed?
“While you were wandering for alms...”
I gave garlands and molasses, O Bhante;
this is the result of that karma that I am experiencing in the world of the gods.
And I have regret, O Bhante; I have failed and am pained.
I did not listen to the Dhamma.
Well-taught by the King of Dhamma—
this I say to you, O Blessed One,
for anyone who has compassion for me.
“Exhort them to those teachings well-expounded by the King of Dhamma—
those who possess faith in the Buddha.”
And in the Dhamma and the Jewel of the Saṅgha;
they outshine me in lifespan, fame, and glory.
“In radiance and beauty, other gods are far superior; they possess greater supernormal power than I.
Thus ends the second discourse on the Radiant Mansion.
